page: OVHcloud r3-16 is a memory-optimized cloud server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. The hardware profile is built on the x86_64 architecture using an AMD EPYC processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. It provides 2 dedicated physical cores mapped to 2 vCPUs without multithreading, alongside 16.0 GB of system memory. This configuration achieves an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. Storage is supplied through a bundled 50 GB local NVMe SSD, and no discrete GPUs are included on the platform.

The CPU architecture incorporates a 32 KB L1 data cache, a 0.5 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB shared L3 cache, supporting hardware instruction sets including AVX, AES, and SHA-NI. In compute benchmarking, the instance demonstrated strong single-core performance in stress-ng with a score of 3075.26, while multi-core stress-ng tests placed in the average tier at 6106.15. Geekbench evaluations recorded a single-core score of 1899.0 and a multi-core score of 3412.0. Memory throughput metrics showed an average transfer capability for large blocks, reaching 61.8 GB/sec in read operations and 41.98 GB/sec in write operations.

Tradeoffs center primarily on raw thread count versus available memory. The dual-core constraint limits overall parallel execution, as reflected by a Passmark CPU score of 5401.69 and 4.9 million Redis SET operations per second. However, the high memory-to-core ratio allows cost-efficient resource provisioning for workloads that require substantial RAM without demanding heavy multi-threaded execution. OVHcloud r3-16 is best suited for lightweight relational databases, in-memory key-value caching layers, data processing workers, and isolated development environments.
description: OVHcloud r3-16 is a memory-optimized cloud instance powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor operating at 2.3 GHz. Provisioned with 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs without simultaneous multithreading, it delivers 16.0 GB of memory for an 8.0 GB per-core allocation. The instance includes a bundled 50 GB local NVMe SSD and operates without discrete GPUs. In benchmark assessments, it displays strong single-core CPU throughput in stress-ng and average memory throughput on large uncached blocks, measuring 61.8 GB/sec read and 41.98 GB/sec write. Multi-threaded throughput is restricted by the two-core limit, reflecting lower scores in parallel compute and database operations. The high memory density relative to compute cores provides effective cost efficiency for memory-centric tasks such as small database instances, in-memory caching systems, and lightweight data pipeline stages.
